body.statement:
For the scaled signed-depth alternatives there are finite constants \(K_0\) and \(B_0\), depending only on \(t_0\), such that, uniformly in \(C\ge1\), \(Q\ge1\), \(T\ge1\), \(v\in\{-1,+1\}\), and every positive-probability observed history,
\[
 E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =vc_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v,
 \qquad q_t^v\le K_0\alpha^Q,
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\|\,
 \mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le B_0T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}.
\]
The bounds include every stationary initial window \(t\le Q\) and reveal neither reset times nor hidden depths.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(p:=L^{-1}\) and \(\bar c:=c_0/\gamma_0=(1-\alpha)/4\).  Then \(0<\bar c<1-\alpha\), because \((1-\alpha)/4<1-\alpha\).  All action words have positive behavior probability, and all reward emissions have probability at least \((1-\bar c)/2>0\), so every conditional probability below is well defined.

We first identify the conditional reward mean.  If \(t>Q\), the event \(J_t=Q\) forces an uninterrupted episode beginning at depth zero at time \(t-Q\).  The preceding \(Q\) rewards in that episode occur at depths \(0,\ldots,Q-1\), hence are fair scaled Rademacher variables and carry no information about its reset sign.  That sign has mean \(\varepsilon_C\), and its mean is retained precisely when all actions \(A_{t-Q},\ldots,A_{t-1}\) equal one.  If \(t\le Q\), the same event forces \(J_1=Q-t+1\) and \(t-1\) uninterrupted advances.  By the behavior-stationary law in \(\mathrm{lem{:}scaled\text{-}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}radius}\), the initial sign conditional on that depth has mean \(\varepsilon_Cp^{Q-t+1}\); the observed preceding rewards are again nonterminal and fair.  Since \(\ell_t=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), both cases give
\[
 E_v[U_t\mathbf1\{J_t=Q\}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v.
\]
The reward kernel then yields
\[
 E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =vc_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v. \tag{13}
\]

We next bound the posterior terminal probability.  Condition also on the realized action window, which is legitimate because the constant observed state and \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\) make behavior actions independent Bernoulli\((p)\) draws under both alternatives.  For \(t>Q\), on \(J_t=Q\) the reward word from \(t-Q\) through \(t-1\) is fair, and its joint numerator conditional on \(\mathcal F_{t-Q-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is
\[
 \Pr_v(J_{t-Q}=0\mid\mathcal F_{t-Q-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\alpha^Q2^{-Q}
 \le\alpha^Q2^{-Q}.
\]
For \(t\le Q\), stationarity and the identity \(w_{Q-t+1}\alpha^{t-1}=w_Q\) make the corresponding numerator \(w_Q2^{-(t-1)}\le\alpha^Q2^{-(t-1)}\).  By the chain rule and (13), the denominator in either case is
\[
 2^{-\ell_t}\prod_{r=t-\ell_t}^{t-1}
 \left\{1+\frac{Y_r}{\gamma_0}\frac{E_v[Y_r\mid\mathcal F_{r-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]}{\gamma_0}\right\}.
\]
The absolute standardized conditional mean is at most \(\bar c q_r^v\), because \(\varepsilon_Ca_r^{(Q)}\le1\).  Therefore
\[
 q_t^v\le\alpha^Q
 \prod_{r=t-\ell_t}^{t-1}(1-\bar c q_r^v)^{-1}. \tag{14}
\]
First using only \(q_r^v\le1\) in (14) gives
\[
 q_t^v\le\left(\frac{\alpha}{1-\bar c}\right)^Q=:r_0^Q,
 \qquad 0<r_0<1. \tag{15}
\]
Substitution of (15) back into (14), together with \(-\log(1-z)\le z/(1-z)\) for \(0\le z<1\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_t^v
 &\le\alpha^Q(1-\bar c r_0^Q)^{-Q}\\
 &\le\alpha^Q\exp\!\left\{
 \frac{\bar c}{1-\bar c}Qr_0^Q\right\}
 \le K_0\alpha^Q,
 \end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
where
\[
 K_0:=\exp\!\left\{\frac{\bar c r_0}{(1-\bar c)(1-r_0)^2}\right\}<\infty.
\]
The last inequality uses \(Qr_0^Q\le\sum_{j\ge1}jr_0^j=r_0/(1-r_0)^2\).  Both \(r_0\) and \(K_0\) depend only on \(\alpha\), hence only on \(t_0\).

It remains to compute observed-path divergence.  Conditional actions have the same law under both alternatives and contribute zero to the likelihood ratio.  Conditional on a common observed history, \(Y_t/\gamma_0\) is Rademacher with means
\[
 \eta_t^v:=\frac{E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]}{\gamma_0}
 =v\bar c\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v.
\]
For Rademacher laws with means \(r,s\), direct substitution into their two point masses and \(\log u\le u-1\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\operatorname{Rad}(r)\|\operatorname{Rad}(s))
 \le\chi^2(\operatorname{Rad}(r)\|\operatorname{Rad}(s))
 =\frac{(r-s)^2}{1-s^2}. \tag{17}
\]
Equations (16)--(17), \(|\eta_t^{-1}|\le\bar c\), and \(q_t^{+1}+q_t^{-1}\le2K_0\alpha^Q\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal L_{+1}(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\|
 \mathcal L_{-1}(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}})\}
 \le\frac{4\bar c^2K_0^2}{1-\bar c^2}
 \varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}(a_t^{(Q)})^2. \tag{18}
\]
Under the plus law the actions remain independent Bernoulli\((p)\), so
\[
 E_{+1}[(a_t^{(Q)})^2]
 =p^{2(Q-\ell_t)}p^{\ell_t}=p^{2Q-\ell_t}\le p^Q=L^{-Q}. \tag{19}
\]
For finite positive-probability paths, the log likelihood ratio is the sum of the conditional log likelihood ratios.  Taking its plus-law expectation, then applying (18)--(19), proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le B_0T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q},
 \qquad
 B_0:=\frac{4\bar c^2K_0^2}{1-\bar c^2}.
\]
The displayed \(B_0\) depends only on \(t_0\) and is independent of \(C,Q,T,M_1,M_2\); scaling by \(\gamma_0\) has canceled from the likelihood calculation.
body.justification: This closes the early kill test and keeps the squared overlap perturbation explicit in the observed-data testing modulus.
body.gap: The proof controls stationary initial windows and hidden reset episodes without revealing latent times.
body.consumer: It supplies the cardinality-uniform two-point divergence for the minimax converse.
